title: Summarize Invoices
prompt: A TypeScript finance page needs totals for paid and unpaid invoices. Write a function that returns { paid, unpaid } where each value is the sum of invoice amounts in that group.

explanation.beginner:
Example: summarizeInvoices([{"amount":10,"paid":true},{"amount":7,"paid":false}]) produces {"paid":10,"unpaid":7}. Choose the numeric contribution of each record, then combine those contributions using the contract’s initial value.

Compare “starts totals at zero”: input [[]] produces {"paid":0,"unpaid":0}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Choose the numeric contribution of each record, then combine those contributions using the contract’s initial value.

Tempting mistake: A count of records is not a sum of their values. Test empty input and a zero-valued record separately.

The reference uses reduce. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “starts totals at zero”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
